purpose: For each sensor/modality: current science state, current confidence tier, pending evidence, decision sensitivity (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), and the explicit decision-flip condition that would change the conclusion. Rules only - no future results are invented or assumed.

sensors.decision_flip_condition: N/A - would require a NEW independent dataset showing a null or negative result under the same capacity-controlled design to materially weaken this tier; no such experiment is planned.
sensors.reason: Two independent datasets, capacity-controlled, consistent direction, disclosed heterogeneity does not reverse the aggregate.

sensors.current_confidence_tier: TIER_B_CONTROLLED_SUPPORT (same-dataset); TIER_C_BOUNDED_SUPPORT (external, via HMC bounded n=7)

HMC-1_strong_external_replication.condition: Full-cohort HMC shows B-A macro-F1 delta of comparable sign and magnitude to Sleep-EDF's own +0.028 (or larger), with a majority of held-out test recordings favoring B, AND the shuffled-EOG control condition remains clearly worse than B (control superiority preserved).
HMC-1_strong_external_replication.implication_if_observed: EOG would be promotable to TIER_A_REPLICATED_SUPPORT and its architecture_implication in results/stage4_scientific_sensor_value_matrix.json could reasonably move from SUPPORTED toward STRONGLY_SUPPORTED_CORE.

HMC-2_near_zero_external_benefit.condition: Full-cohort HMC shows a B-A delta close to zero (e.g. within the seed-to-seed noise band already observed in Sleep-EDF, roughly +/-0.01-0.03 macro-F1) with no clear majority direction across held-out recordings.
HMC-2_near_zero_external_benefit.implication_if_observed: EOG would remain TIER_C_BOUNDED_SUPPORT for external validity - same-dataset support stays TIER_B, but the external claim should downgrade to 'inconclusive at full scale' rather than supportive or negative.

HMC-3_external_negative_result.condition: Full-cohort HMC shows a stable, majority-consistent NEGATIVE B-A delta across held-out recordings (EOG measurably hurts external sleep-stage classification), not attributable to a single-recording artifact.
HMC-3_external_negative_result.implication_if_observed: EOG's architecture candidacy should downgrade toward CONDITIONAL_CANDIDATE or EXPERIMENTAL_CANDIDATE - same-dataset support alone would no longer be sufficient given a real external negative signal, and the burden-vs-evidence case would need re-examination even under a shared-AFE assumption.

sensors.reason: The only external evidence (HMC bounded n=7, 1 test recording) is statistically underpowered to be informative in either direction - a genuinely open question with a large realistic evidence gap.

sensors.pending_evidence: Full ~65-subject ds003838 cohort (quantified: ~93GB/~9.4h additional download, not attempted).

DS-1_sparse_approximately_equals_full.condition: Full-cohort comparison shows sparse (4-channel) EEG performance within a small, consistently-observed margin of full-montage EEG across the majority of subjects, with no subgroup showing a large gap.
DS-1_sparse_approximately_equals_full.implication_if_observed: Would support electrode minimization for the EEG module - a real evidence-based case for a low-channel-count architecture.

DS-2_sparse_materially_worse.condition: Full-cohort comparison shows sparse EEG meaningfully and consistently worse than full montage (a gap well beyond seed/subject noise) across the majority of subjects.
DS-2_sparse_materially_worse.implication_if_observed: Would weaken aggressive EEG channel minimization as a scientifically-supported choice.

DS-3_strong_subject_heterogeneity.condition: Full-cohort comparison shows some subjects with near-equal sparse/full performance and others with a large gap, without a consistent population-level direction.
DS-3_strong_subject_heterogeneity.implication_if_observed: May justify a CONDITIONAL architecture (e.g. adaptive or subject-calibrated channel count) rather than a single universal configuration - this is a real, distinct architecture class worth defining (see results/stage4_architecture_candidate_classes.json).

sensors.reason: n=3 is far too small to distinguish any of these three scenarios; the full cohort is the only evidence that could resolve this.

sensors.decision_flip_condition: Would require a substantially larger held-out test set (current n=4) showing a stable positive direction - no such experiment is planned, and prior sprints already established the current result's fragility without reversing its aggregate sign.
sensors.reason: Consistently negative aggregate across the tested design; no currently-planned Stage-3 work would materially change this.

sensors.decision_flip_condition: Would require a larger or outlier-robust-redesigned cohort to resolve the aggregate-vs-per-subject-direction tension (7/10 subjects favor B despite a negative aggregate mean) - no such experiment is currently planned.
sensors.reason: The ambiguity is real and disclosed, but no currently-planned Stage-3 experiment would resolve it further; new experimental design would be required, which is out of current scope.

sensors.decision_flip_condition: Would require a different target endpoint, a different site (abdominal/arm), or a substantially larger cohort to move past subject-9 sensitivity - none of these are currently planned Stage-3 experiments.
sensors.reason: Both key comparisons (A-B, C-B) are subject-9-influenced; no currently-planned Stage-3 work addresses this specific gap.

sensors.pending_evidence: None currently planned beyond the existing interaction experiment.
sensors.decision_flip_condition: Would require more optimization seeds or a second dataset's interaction test - not currently planned.
sensors.reason: Interaction magnitude is small relative to its own seed-level noise; no near-term evidence would resolve it.

sensors.current_science_state: No governing Stage-3 experiment exists for either.
sensors.pending_evidence: No experiment currently planned or in progress for either modality.
sensors.decision_flip_condition: Any future Stage-3-equivalent experiment testing either modality against a controlled baseline would immediately move it out of TIER_P - currently rated MEDIUM (not LOW) because, unlike the other pending items above, there is no evidence at all to anchor a confidence judgment, so any new experiment (even a small one) could be more decision-relevant than incremental evidence on an already-tested modality.
sensors.reason: Complete absence of governing evidence, not a specific pending experiment with a known scope.
